flux_evidence: Core architecture is frozen, but the ecosystem layer keeps producing real gaps: Pony shipped a non-SDXL V7 successor unmentioned in the skill, and the SDXL/Anima trainer boundary keeps moving.

findings.claim: The skill's checkpoint table and lora-training.md base table present 'Pony Diffusion V6 XL' as simply 'Pony,' with no indication of a newer non-SDXL Pony generation.
findings.reality: Pony Diffusion V7 shipped 2025-10-08: a 7B AuraFlow-based model (not an SDXL finetune), with its own LoRA pool (SimpleTuner, not kohya/OneTrainer) and a new tag+description prompting scheme replacing score_9. V6 remains dominant for production/LoRA work today because V7's ecosystem is still immature, but the omission mirrors exactly the gap the skill already flags for Anima.
findings.fix_hint: SKILL.md checkpoint table ~L66 and anime-axis callout ~L71; references/checkpoints-and-loras.md §3; references/lora-training.md §1 base table — add a Pony-V7 callout parallel to the existing Anima paragraph, noting V6 remains the practical pick until V7's LoRA pool matures.

findings.claim: lora-training.md §8 says SDXL weight-noising params are 'still being worked out' (open/unstable status).
findings.reality: The ai-toolkit-perceptual repo now lists SDXL as 'Supported' for both weight noising and perceptual anchors, but only gives a generic sigma range (0.01-0.017) with no SDXL-tuned recipe distinct from Flux/Z-Image — so the claim should soften from 'not yet worked out' to 'generic range applies, no SDXL-specific tuning published yet.'

findings.claim: lora-training.md §2/§7 doesn't mention kohya_ss's LoKr/LoHa engine support scope for SDXL vs. newer bases.
findings.reality: kohya_ss sd-scripts changelog now lists LoKr/LoHa support explicitly for 'SDXL/Anima' together, plus multi-resolution bucketing — confirming the trainer now natively spans both bases named in the skill's base-selection table.
findings.fix_hint: references/lora-training.md §2 Tools / §7 Style LoRAs, LyCORIS note.

findings.claim: checkpoints-and-loras.md §2 names 'Juggernaut XL' generically with 'v9/v10/v11 line — check current.'
findings.reality: The current Juggernaut line (v10 / 'Juggernaut X') now ships as two separate checkpoints, SFW and NSFW, rather than one unified file — a structural change the hedge doesn't capture, though it correctly avoided pinning a version number.

findings.claim: The anima-as-illustrious-challenger watchlist item asks whether Anima's LoRA pool and finetune ecosystem have matured.
findings.reality: Third-party Anima finetunes are now shipping on Civitai (e.g. 'CyberRealistic Anima v7.0 Turbo'), evidence the base ecosystem is growing past the initial CircleStone release — a data point for the anima skill to track, not yet a verdict on displacing Illustrious.
findings.fix_hint: Defer to the `anima` skill's own freshness entry; sdxl's references/lora-training.md §1 Anima row can stay as-is.

new_techniques.what: Civitai's own on-site LoRA trainer is a documented alternative to local kohya_ss/OneTrainer for SDXL/Illustrious, with its own quirks: set repeats=1 and scale batch size instead (inflating repeats 'lies to the optimizer'), only flip-augmentation is available, and Prodigy always trains the text encoder regardless of settings.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: It's a no-local-GPU path readers may reach for, but its defaults and cost model (buzz-per-step bands) differ enough from kohya/OneTrainer that following this skill's kohya-flavored advice verbatim there would misfire.

new_techniques.what: Pony V7's LoRA training runs on SimpleTuner against the AuraFlow architecture, not kohya_ss/OneTrainer, and V7's own team flags its prompting as still inconsistent pending a V7.1 fix.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Anyone told to 'train a Pony LoRA' needs routing to a completely different toolchain and base once V6 stops being the answer, the same fork-in-the-road the skill already handles for Anima.

new_techniques.what: neonkisu published a fuller companion article on the 0.33 identity ratio that spells out putting body-descriptor tokens (e.g. build/height phrases) directly in identity-emphasis captions, not just in-context ones.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Confirms and sharpens a nuance already present in the skill's captioning section rather than introducing a new mechanism — worth a citation update, not a rewrite.

add.claim: Pony Diffusion V7 (AuraFlow, 7B, non-SDXL) shipped 2025-10-08 with its own LoRA pool and prompting scheme; V6 XL remains the practical pick for SDXL-ecosystem work while V7's tooling matures.
add.where: SKILL.md checkpoint table + anime-axis callout; references/checkpoints-and-loras.md §3; references/lora-training.md §1
add.check: Has V7's LoRA pool and prompt-consistency (V7.1) matured enough to displace V6 as the default anime/furry recommendation? Track alongside anima-as-illustrious-challenger — SDXL's anime axis now has two non-SDXL challengers, not one.

amend.change: ai-toolkit-perceptual now lists SDXL as 'Supported' for weight noising (not just depth anchoring), but only with the generic sigma range (0.01-0.017), no SDXL-tuned config. Update the check to ask specifically whether an SDXL-specific sigma/config has since been published, distinct from the generic range.
kohya_ss sd-scripts changelog now explicitly names SDXL/Anima together for LoKr/LoHa support — note this convergence next check and see if OneTrainer/ai-toolkit have matched it.
